A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HybGRAG research. Their main text, figures, tables, algorithm, and appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching of retained, added, and relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original STARK retrieval experiments, CRAG question-answering results, ablations, and case studies, including Tables 5–7 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds the single-agent comparison in Table 7.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same retriever bank, router, validator, commenter, and iterative feedback procedure. The single-agent variant is introduced as a comparison baseline; HybGRAG itself is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate retrieval on STARK-MAG and STARK-PRIME and end-to-end question answering on the same five-domain CRAG coverage. The new single-agent experiment reuses STARK-MAG.

E2.justification: v2 adds the evaluated 'Router for SR' single-agent baseline in Table 7, alongside the existing Hybrid Retrieval Module and HybGRAG. Comparator membership in the main STARK and CRAG benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated test splits, sample counts, metrics, backbone and embedding models, two-hop extraction limit, and four-iteration configuration remain unchanged. The added baseline comparison does not specify a separate change to the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Section 4.1.2 and new Table 7 test whether using the router alone for self-reflection matches HybGRAG's separate critic design. This adds one targeted ablation; existing context, example-count, iteration, model-size, oracle, and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The new comparison uses the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports Router for SR scores of 0.6206 Hit@1, 0.7069 Hit@5, 0.6187 Recall@20, and 0.6587 MRR on STARK-MAG. Its Hybrid Retrieval Module and HybGRAG rows reuse existing values. Main benchmark and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 adds notation expressing D as the union of entity-associated documents D_i, making an already-described relationship explicit. This is a notational clarification without a substantive new assumption, mathematical result, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution list, and conclusion retain the agentic, adaptive, interpretable, and effective claims, including the average 51% relative Hit@1 improvement. The new comparison provides additional support without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds limitations concerning unexplored retrieval alternatives, limited domain-adaptation advantages, and random in-context example selection. It also interprets the new single-agent comparison as supporting specialized corrective feedback and removes the explicit CRAG base-model robustness statement.

D1.justification: The new Limitations section discloses that the commenter selects in-context experiences randomly, which v1 did not specify. This is additional implementation information, without evidence of a changed selection procedure. Existing hardware, prompts, settings, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Qiao et al.'s AutoAct citation and revises the discussion to distinguish agentic from self-reflective LLMs. It expands the explanation of their difficulties with HQA, while retaining the broader Graph RAG positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical and terminology corrections, clarifies benchmark descriptions, rewrites parts of Sections 2, 4.2, and 5, and adds a Limitations section. The overall narrative structure and most appendix text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains explicit textual/relational aspect labels, Figure 4 is resized with revised ticks, and Table 7 is added. The CRAG cost table moves from main-text Table 9 to appendix Table 14 with unchanged values. The overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The single-agent comparison provides targeted additional support for the critic design. Explicit limitations, the newly disclosed example-selection detail, and clearer Figure 1 improve transparency and explanation. These are useful but limited gains; the core method, principal results, and existing evaluation settings remain unchanged.
